messages:
olivia: Heads-up — ran into a hole in our API key model during a dry-run. If an org-scoped key can mint or directly call project-scoped APIs, we end up with unexpected cross-project impersonation surface. Is this expected?
kevin: Can you outline the exact flow you're worried about? org-key -> service -> project resource?
sara: This sounds like scoping. Last RFC leaned us toward org keys for infra convenience + project tokens for product workloads. Did the dry-run use a minting endpoint?
aj: Short take: we need a clear token shape and delegation chain. At minimum a scoped claim (e.g., scope: ["org:123"] or "project:xyz") and an aud/iss pair.
sanjay: Also consider key-proofing: rotate KIDs and optionally require client certs for mint endpoints. Example token body we saw in the test: 
```
{
  "kid": "org-123/key-1",
  "sub": "service:deploy-bot",
  "scope": ["org:123"],
  "exp": 1912345678
}
```
security-bot: :warning: Security note: org-wide keys are a large blast radius. Recommend forbidding direct org-key calls to project admin endpoints; only allow delegation to short-lived project-scoped tokens.
olivia: The practical problem: a bunch of infra scripts assume org keys for cross-project ops today. We need a migration that doesn't break CI. My proposal: allow org keys only to mint ephemeral project-scoped tokens via a dedicated STS endpoint, require strong auth (mTLS + policy check), and emit audit events that show original actor + delegation chain.
kevin: Agreed. Enforcement idea: new endpoint POST /v1/token/delegate that only accepts org keys, issues tokens with max ttl 5m and a mandatory "delegated_for" claim. The service checks both the token and the delegation header.
aj: Add to that: require the caller to present a client cert (mTLS) and be on an allowlist for that org. Also require a "reason" field for audit.
sara: Ops asks for an admin UI to list active delegated tokens and revoke them. Also we should surface delegation events in the Console (>audit view).
olivia: I'll draft a short RFC PR that includes: 1) token shape changes, 2) delegation API, 3) audit event schema, 4) migration plan + deprecation timeline, 5) SDK changes. Who wants to co-author?
kevin: I'll take mTLS + policy enforcement section.
sanjay: I'll add SDK + infra template updates, and write the regression tests for scoping.
security-bot: Reminder: please spin up a tracking ticket in our tracker (SEC-XXXX) and tag the RFC.
olivia: Thanks — will put a first draft up this afternoon. If we can get the migration timeline locked this week we can start communicating to customers that use org keys. :thumbsup:
